v.rationale: All three use the same modern approach: an attribute-based command, a #[Scope] on User, a nullable timestamp with a datetime cast, and the Schedule facade in routes/console.php. The deciding difference is the logging requirement. Laravel sends scheduled command output to /dev/null by default (checked in vendor Event.php), and impl-2 sets no output target, so its daily number never reaches the logs. That is a real requirement miss, even though impl-2 otherwise has the cleanest code and good tests. impl-1 and impl-3 both append the output to storage/logs. impl-1 ranks above impl-3 because its tests are stronger: frozen time, the exact-cutoff boundary, the empty-value case and a factory state. Its weaknesses are an unlabelled bare-number output and some test ceremony. impl-3 prints the ungrammatical '1 users', uses a heavier Validator, leaves the imports out of order, and does not freeze time or test the boundary.
